Card checkout on ($5-$1,000, 2.9% + $0.30).

Staking is built but switched off (health: staking.enabled false). The 'burns' on the site are rCREDIT (their $1 credit token), not $RAETO.

Token (/token): 'Keepers and relayers bond $MERY to run Meryal... a fault a contract can check costs 10% of it. No trading fee is redistributed: no buyback, no burn tax, no revenue share.' Bonds contract 0xf822a1Bb: 0 events.

Usage since contracts went live 5 Nov 07:09 UTC: pool 0x4FFCAD6a 5 transactions, all from their operator 0x499923aa; vault, sealed, credit, bonds, registry, settler: 0 events. Older contracts: pool 10 tx all operator; vault 4 tx from 2 wallets (1 operator).
Paid AI API (/api/v1/models): one model 'meryal/sandbox' ('answers about Meryal, deterministic, for the demo'); payment 'verified, not settled (no facilitator configured)'.

SDK shown on /developers and /agents (@meryal/rx402) is not on npm. No public GitHub found, though the site says Apache 2.0. 'Live beta. Not audited.' Proof setup run by the operator until a public ceremony.

Scanner corrections: 'buyback' (+10) misread of 'no buyback' (fixed 6 Nov); 'API keys' (+10) misread of 'no API key' (fixed 6 Nov); 'no working app' is wrong: app pages exist (/borrow, /credit), but nobody outside the team uses them.

Trading 6 Nov ~05:30 UTC: a bot (157k transactions) plus 5 near-new wallets holding identical 0.4950 ETH balances bought in the same seconds; this looks manufactured, not demand (GeckoTerminal trades + RPC).
Domain is new (in the ShortDot new-domain list for 29-30 Oct, github.com/phishdestroy/shortdot-evidence); .sbs is a cheap ending often used for scams: context, not an accusation.
